title: Auditing & Compliance with pgaudit
description: Track DDL and DML operations for compliance audits using the official pgaudit extension.

data.text: Standard PostgreSQL logging is designed for debugging, not compliance auditing. **`pgaudit` (PostgreSQL Audit Extension)** produces structured, tamper-resistant audit logs that fulfill compliance mandates by recording who accessed which tables and executed what statements.

data.title: Configuring pgaudit in postgresql.conf
data.content: Auditing role changes, DDL modifications, and table reads.
data.code:
# In postgresql.conf:
shared_preload_libraries = 'pgaudit'
pgaudit.log = 'role, ddl, write'
pgaudit.log_catalog = off
pgaudit.log_parameter = on

data.text: pgaudit logs what happened, who did it, and which objects were touched. Different classes of events are enabled separately: `READ` for SELECT, `WRITE` for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, `DDL`, `ROLE`, and `FUNCTION`. Auditing every read on a busy system generates enormous logs, so scope it to the tables that hold regulated data.

data.title: Enable pgaudit and scope it
data.content: Reading is audited only for the sensitive table, while DDL and role changes are always logged. `log_parameter` records bind values for forensic detail.

data.title: Interview angle: auditing is a pipeline, not a setting
data.text: A compliant audit trail needs capture, secure transport, retention, and review. Turning on pgaudit is only capture. The logs must go somewhere tamper-evident and outside the DBA's control (a central log store with restricted write access), be retained for the required period, and be reviewed or alerted on. Saying that the highest-privilege users are exactly the ones whose actions must be audited is a strong point — the DBA is usually the person you most need to record.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `pgaudit` satisfies SOC 2, HIPAA, and PCI-DSS audit logging requirements.
Records user, session, command tag, statement text, and parameters.
Route audit logs to centralized SIEM tools like Splunk or Datadog.
